title: win+v cannot work!

status.label: Current-build local reproduction warranted
status.detail: The issue has a maintainer reproduction and detailed 2024 control evidence: clipboard history fails when Ctrl (Left) is remapped, while removing that mapping restores paste.

next_action: Reproduce on a current build with the Ctrl (Left) mapping and control case, then decide how external synthetic shortcuts should interact with remapping.

judgment.rationale: The issue has a maintainer-reproduced historical failure and specific follow-up reports. In 2024, a commenter isolated the failure to remapping Ctrl (Left), showed that removing that mapping restores clipboard history paste, and supplied a keyboard-event trace. Closed issue #35345 explicitly points back here as the duplicate. Current main marks Keyboard Manager’s own injected events with its private extra-info flag, but the issue does not establish how Windows Clipboard History’s generated Ctrl+V is marked or whether the behavior persists today. A maintainer can test the existing steps before a safe design is selected.
evidence: A maintainer said they reproduced the issue in 2021 and attributed it to Windows Clipboard History sending Ctrl+V through the active window while Keyboard Manager remaps the keys.
A 2024 report says remapping Ctrl (Left) causes the failure while Ctrl (Right) is OK; unbinding Ctrl (Left) restores Win+V paste.
The 2024 reporter provided a QMK event trace showing the clipboard-history selection sequence produces Esc/V key events instead of pasting.
Closed issue #35345 explicitly says it is a duplicate of #14556 and describes the same clipboard-history/left-modifier remapping conflict.

Current KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp uses Keyboard Manager-specific extra-info markers to identify its own injected input; the issue does not show whether Windows Clipboard History events carry a distinguishable marker.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the Ctrl (Left) control case on a current build and verify whether Windows Clipboard History input is transformed by the remap before deciding a safe policy for externally generated shortcuts.

fix_assessment.rationale: The historical behavior is well supported, but no current-build retest confirms it still occurs and the issue does not establish a safe general rule for remapping externally generated input. Verify the control case before proposing a change that could affect other applications or accessibility tools.

issue_context.summary: Windows Clipboard History opens with Win+V but selecting an item reportedly sends literal V/Alt-menu behavior instead of pasting when Ctrl (Left) is remapped.
known_information: The original report remaps CapsLock to Ctrl and Ctrl to CapsLock and says clipboard history selection yields V instead of pasted content.
A maintainer reproduced the issue in 2021 and noted that Clipboard History sends Ctrl+V to the active window, where Keyboard Manager remapping can intercept it.
A 2024 comment isolates the behavior to a Ctrl (Left) remap and says removing that mapping restores Win+V paste; Ctrl (Right) was reported to work.
The 2024 discussion includes a QMK trace of the clipboard-history selection event and a workaround using a shortcut remap.
Closed #35345 is explicitly marked as a duplicate of #14556.
Current source identifies Keyboard Manager-generated input using its own extra-info marker; no issue evidence establishes how Clipboard History input is tagged on current Windows.
inferences: Windows Clipboard History may inject a shortcut that the normal remap path treats like user input, but the exact event flags and current-build behavior remain unverified.
Ignoring every injected event could affect software-generated shortcuts beyond Clipboard History, so a change needs a deliberate policy and current reproduction.
issue_context.analysis: The detailed historical reports justify a maintainer reproduction rather than another generic log request. Use the Ctrl (Left) mapping as the discriminating variable and verify the no-mapping control; do not treat #35345 as separate work or assume all injected input should bypass remapping.
initial_investigation: Read all 17 comments, including the maintainer reproduction, 0.77 report, Ctrl (Left) control, QMK trace, and workaround.
Read closed #35345 and confirmed it explicitly redirects to #14556.
Inspected current KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp: Keyboard Manager-generated inputs are identified by its own extra-info flag; no current-build report confirms Windows Clipboard History behavior.

actions.label: Reproduce Win+V with Ctrl remapped
actions.note: Historical reports provide a specific control case; verify it on a current build before designing event-filter changes.

reproduce.title: Verify Windows Clipboard History with Ctrl (Left) remapped
prerequisites: Windows Clipboard History enabled with at least one item
A text editor or other paste target
setup: Configure CapsLock to send Ctrl (Left) and Ctrl (Left) to send CapsLock, matching the reported setup.
steps: Focus a paste target and press Win+V.
Select a clipboard item and observe whether its contents are pasted or literal V/Alt-menu behavior appears.
As a control, remove the Ctrl (Left) remap and repeat the same Win+V selection.
reproduce.expected_result: Selecting an item should paste its contents; the historical report says the Ctrl (Left) remap instead produces V/Alt-menu behavior, while removing the mapping restores paste.
